description: This topic introduces the types of photographs, their parts, and how to read, interpret and use photographs to study geographical features.

mcq.questionText: A photograph taken from the ground while the camera is held in the hand or placed on a stand is called a:
mcq.explanation: A ground photograph is taken from a position on or near the surface of the earth, not from the air.

mcq.questionText: An aerial photograph taken with the camera pointing straight down so the lens is at right angles to the ground is known as a:
mcq.explanation: In a vertical aerial photograph the camera axis points directly downward, giving a map-like view of the area.

mcq.questionText: Which type of aerial photograph is taken with the camera tilted at an angle so that part of the horizon may be seen?
mcq.explanation: An oblique aerial photograph is taken with the camera tilted, so it shows the sides of features and sometimes the horizon.

mcq.questionText: The part of a photograph that is nearest to the camera and appears at the bottom is called the:
mcq.explanation: The foreground is the area closest to the camera, usually shown at the bottom of the photograph where objects appear largest.

mcq.questionText: In a ground photograph, the part that is furthest from the camera and appears at the top is the:
mcq.explanation: The background is the most distant part of a photograph and is shown at the top, where objects appear smallest.

mcq.questionText: Which part of a photograph lies between the foreground and the background?
mcq.explanation: The middle ground is the central part of a photograph found between the foreground and the background.

mcq.questionText: Which type of photograph gives a view most similar to a topographical map?
mcq.explanation: A vertical aerial photograph shows features from directly above, giving a plan view that closely resembles a map.

mcq.questionText: One main difference between a photograph and a map is that a map:

options.text: Shows the actual colours of features
Uses conventional symbols and a key
Records features exactly as they appear

mcq.explanation: A map uses agreed conventional symbols explained in a key, while a photograph shows features as they actually appear.

mcq.questionText: On a ground or oblique photograph, objects that are far from the camera appear:

options.text: The same size as those nearby

mcq.explanation: Because of perspective, distant objects appear smaller while nearer objects in the foreground appear larger.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of a photograph over a map?

options.text: It shows the true appearance and colour of features
It always has a fixed scale
It can show the whole world at once

mcq.explanation: A photograph records the real appearance, shape and colour of features, which a map shows only with symbols.

mcq.questionText: When estimating the size of an object in a photograph, it is helpful to compare it with an object of known size, such as a:
mcq.explanation: Familiar objects of known size, like people or vehicles, act as a guide for estimating the size of other features.

mcq.questionText: Which feature in a photograph would most likely be identified as a settlement?

options.text: A group of houses arranged together
A wide stretch of open water

mcq.explanation: A cluster of houses or buildings grouped together indicates a settlement where people live.

mcq.questionText: A photograph is generally not useful for showing:

options.text: The names of towns and rivers

mcq.explanation: A photograph cannot label features with names, so place names and other written information must come from a map.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a use of photographs in the study of geography?

options.text: Replacing the need to visit any place
Studying land use and human activities in an area
Measuring the exact height of land above sea level
Drawing the legend of a map

mcq.explanation: Photographs help geographers observe and study land use, vegetation, settlement and human activities in an area.

mcq.questionText: A farmer wants to compare how the size of a maize farm has changed over several years using two vertical aerial photographs taken at different times. This shows that photographs are useful for:

options.text: Showing changes in features over time
Recording the names of the farms
Giving the exact temperature of the area

mcq.explanation: Photographs taken of the same place at different times allow comparison and study of changes such as the growth of farms or towns.

fib.questionText: A photograph taken from a high position such as an aeroplane is called an _____ photograph.
fib.explanation: Aerial photographs are taken from the air, usually from an aircraft or other flying device.

fib.questionText: The two main types of aerial photographs are vertical and _____ photographs.
fib.explanation: Aerial photographs are either vertical (taken straight down) or oblique (taken at an angle).

fib.questionText: The part of a photograph closest to the camera is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The foreground is the nearest part, found at the bottom of the photograph.

fib.questionText: The most distant part of a photograph, found at the top, is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The background is the farthest part of the photograph where objects appear smallest.

fib.questionText: The part of a photograph between the foreground and the background is the _____.
fib.explanation: The middle ground is the central area lying between the foreground and the background.

fib.questionText: A vertical aerial photograph gives a view that is most similar to a _____.
fib.explanation: Because it is taken from directly above, a vertical aerial photograph shows a plan view like a map.

fib.questionText: To estimate the size of features in a photograph, we compare them with objects of _____ size such as people or cars.
fib.explanation: Familiar objects of known size serve as a reference for estimating the size of unknown features.

fib.questionText: Unlike a map, a photograph shows features in their true colours and real _____.
fib.explanation: A photograph captures the actual appearance and colour of features, while a map uses symbols.

fib.questionText: On an oblique aerial photograph, the line where the sky appears to meet the land is called the _____.
fib.explanation: Oblique photographs often include the horizon because the camera is tilted at an angle.

fib.questionText: Photographs taken of the same area at different times help geographers to study _____ over time.
fib.explanation: Comparing photographs from different periods shows how features such as towns and farms have changed.

tf.questionText: A ground photograph is taken from a position on or near the surface of the earth.
tf.explanation: Ground photographs are taken from the ground level rather than from the air.

tf.questionText: A vertical aerial photograph is taken with the camera pointing straight down to the ground.
tf.explanation: In a vertical aerial photograph the camera axis is at right angles to the ground, looking straight down.

tf.questionText: In a photograph, objects in the background appear larger than objects in the foreground.
tf.explanation: Objects in the foreground appear larger; those in the background appear smaller because they are far away.

tf.questionText: An oblique aerial photograph is taken with the camera tilted at an angle to the ground.
tf.explanation: An oblique aerial photograph is taken at an angle, so it shows the sides of features and sometimes the horizon.

tf.questionText: A photograph uses conventional symbols and a key to show features.
tf.explanation: Maps use symbols and a key, while photographs show features as they actually appear.

tf.questionText: A photograph can show the actual colours of features such as green vegetation and brown soil.
tf.explanation: One advantage of a photograph is that it records the true colours and appearance of features.

tf.questionText: Place names and the height of land above sea level can be read directly from a photograph.
tf.explanation: A photograph cannot give names or exact heights; such information must come from a map.

tf.questionText: Comparing features in a photograph with people or vehicles helps in estimating their size.
tf.explanation: Objects of known size, like people or cars, are used as a guide to estimate the size of other features.

tf.questionText: Photographs are useless for studying land use and human activities in an area.
tf.explanation: Photographs are very useful for studying land use, settlement, vegetation and other human activities.

tf.questionText: Two photographs of the same place taken at different times can be used to study changes in the landscape.
tf.explanation: Comparing photographs from different periods reveals changes such as the growth of towns or clearing of forests.

summary.questionText: Main types of photographs by position of camera
summary.explanation: Ground photographs are taken from the surface, while aerial photographs are taken from the air.
Vertical photos look straight down, oblique photos are taken at an angle.

summary.questionText: The three parts of a photograph
summary.explanation: These run from the nearest part at the bottom to the farthest part at the top.

summary.correctAnswer: The part nearest the camera, at the bottom
summary.explanation: Objects in the foreground appear largest because they are closest.

summary.correctAnswer: The most distant part, at the top
summary.explanation: Objects in the background appear smallest because they are farthest away.

summary.questionText: How distance affects the size of objects in a photograph
summary.correctAnswer: Near objects look large, distant objects look small
summary.explanation: This effect of perspective helps in estimating size and distance.

summary.questionText: Way of estimating size of features in a photograph
summary.correctAnswer: Compare with objects of known size like people or cars
summary.explanation: Familiar objects act as a reference scale for size estimation.

summary.questionText: Main difference between a photograph and a map
summary.correctAnswer: A photo shows real appearance; a map uses symbols and a key
summary.explanation: Photographs record true colour and appearance, while maps represent features with symbols.

summary.questionText: Aerial photograph that resembles a map
summary.explanation: It gives a plan view from directly above, similar to a topographical map.

summary.correctAnswer: Studying land use, settlement, vegetation and changes over time
summary.explanation: Photographs help observe features and human activities and compare changes across time.

hoq.questionText: A student looks at an oblique aerial photograph of a town and notices that the buildings near the bottom are very large and clear, while those near the top are small and crowded together. What is the best explanation for this difference?

options.text: The buildings near the top are actually smaller than those at the bottom
The buildings at the top are in the background, so they appear smaller due to distance
The camera was faulty when taking the photograph
Larger buildings are always placed in the foreground of towns

hoq.explanation: In an oblique photograph, features in the background are farther from the camera and so appear smaller and more crowded, even if their real sizes are similar.

hoq.questionText: A geographer wants to find out the exact names of villages, the height of hills in metres, and the true direction between two points in an area. Which source should she mainly rely on, and why?

options.text: A ground photograph, because it shows true colours
An oblique photograph, because it shows the horizon
A map, because it gives names, heights and direction using symbols and a scale
A vertical photograph, because it looks like a map

hoq.explanation: Names, exact heights and directions cannot be read from a photograph; a map provides them through symbols, contour lines, a scale and a north direction.

hoq.questionText: Two vertical aerial photographs of the same farming area were taken ten years apart. The newer one shows more houses and fewer trees than the older one. What can a geographer best conclude from comparing them?

options.text: The newer photograph was taken from a higher position
The area has experienced settlement growth and clearing of forest over time
The camera changed the colours of the features
Photographs cannot be used to study change

hoq.explanation: Comparing photographs of the same place taken at different times reveals changes; more houses and fewer trees show settlement growth and loss of forest.
